::: {.tut-standfirst}
Wrong coordinates are one of the biggest sources of problems in biodiversity data. Saíra helps you find them and review them visually on the map.
:::

## What Saíra checks

From <span class="term">decimalLatitude</span> and <span class="term">decimalLongitude</span>, the app flags the most common problems:

- **Missing** — records with no coordinate.
- **Swapped** — latitude and longitude exchanged (a classic that throws the point to the other side of the world).
- **Out of range** — impossible values (latitude beyond ±90, longitude beyond ±180).
- **Incompatible with expectation** — points falling in the sea for terrestrial records, or far from the stated country.

## Reviewing on the map

```{=html}
<ol class="steps">
  <li><strong>See the distribution.</strong>
    <p>Points appear on the map, colored by status. Clusters outside the expected area stand out.</p></li>
  <li><strong>Fix the swaps.</strong>
    <p>For coordinates detected as swapped, Saíra offers a one-click lat/lon swap.</p></li>
  <li><strong>Handle the missing ones.</strong>
    <p>Records without a coordinate can be filled in from the locality or marked as not georeferenced.</p></li>
</ol>
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Datum and precision
Record the <span class="term">geodeticDatum</span> (for example, <em>WGS84</em>) and, when you know it, the uncertainty in meters (<span class="term">coordinateUncertaintyInMeters</span>). This greatly increases the scientific value of the data.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Coordinate sign in Brazil
Most of Brazil has **negative latitude and longitude**. Positive coordinates where the southern/western hemisphere was expected are a strong sign of a sign error or a swap.
:::
